source_filter.description: Knowledge-store sources this plan's retrieval is scoped to, in the order the caller named them (primary first), de-duplicated. Defaults to the repository's own source plus 'proposed-knowledge', the dedicated source steward-accepted findings ingest under -- a plan scoped to the repository source alone silently returned nothing from the steward-accepted half of the store. Retyped from a bare string when `--source` became repeatable; that retype took schema_version 6 -> 7.

matched_routes.description: Routes that matched, each with why it matched: the keywords, keyword_groups, and path pattern/file pairs that fired. Same shape as matched_risks -- both resolve to one definition so the two cannot drift apart.

matched_risks.description: Risk rules that matched, in the same shape as matched_routes.

undeclared_workflow_shape_routes.description: Optional signal (#214, finishing #210): the ids of matched routes that declared no 'workflow_shape' at all, in match order -- the order routing matched them, NOT sorted. Such a route contributes no delivery shape to the plan's 'workflow' field, so the plan can fall back to 'unclassified' by omission rather than by judgment -- exactly the defect #210 fixed for this repository's own routing.json. routing.schema.json deliberately keeps 'workflow_shape' OPTIONAL so a project-local routing overlay (.agents/orchestration/routing-overlay.json) written before #210 still validates, and validate_routing_config checks only the value, never the presence; requiring it would break every existing overlay that adds a route, a trade considered and rejected. This reports instead. 'unclassified' is a declaration and never appears here -- only a missing, null, or empty field does. Only MATCHED routes appear; a configured route that did not match is never listed. Adding this field incremented schema_version 5 -> 6. It is optional and omitted when empty, but that is NOT the 'optional and not emitted by default' carve-out RUNBOOK.md's 'When schema_version increments' rule grants 'provenance': the carve-out works because the consumer never sees the field, whereas an overlay consumer -- the exact population this signal exists for -- sees this one unconditionally, and their pinned copy of this closed schema would reject the plan while it truthfully reported the version that copy claims to handle. At 6 they fail on this const instead, an error naming the real cause.

kernel_mutation_gate_id.description: Cross-reference to the Agentic SDLC kernel's own contracts/mutation-gates.json id, when one exists for this cadre-side human_gate id. The kernel stays the authoritative definition source; this is a pointer, not a duplicated definition. Null when cadre has no kernel mutation-gate counterpart (e.g. accountable-human-escalation).

source_filter.description: The sources each request in this block retrieves from. Mirrors inputs.source_filter; every entry appears as its own `--source` argument in each request's invocation args.

runtime.description: args[0] is an executable `cadre` wrapper, executed directly. Was "python" through schema_version 7, when args[0] named the knowledge store's `src/cli.py` and the runner supplied its own probed interpreter; the store moved to Go and that script no longer exists.

resolution.description: The path is resolved from the producing platform checkout, never from a resolved roster root (PP-FR-5).

provenance.description: Optional, additive suite-input provenance binding (idea #7). Distinct from and complementary to dispatch_fingerprint: dispatch_fingerprint is a self-consistency checksum over this plan's own emitted content (excludes generated_at and provenance itself); provenance binds the plan to the exact catalog.yaml/routing-configuration content, and best-effort git commit identity, that produced it, independently verifiable without trusting the generating process. Absent entirely on plans built without a matching on-disk catalog/routing file (e.g. in-process fixtures/tests) -- not required at the top level, so plans generated before this field existed remain valid.

overlay_applied.description: Reserved for idea #6 (project-local routing overlay). Currently dormant: select_agents.py's dispatch-plan call path never resolves an overlay, so this and the sibling overlay_* fields are always absent, never fabricated.

runner_capabilities_content_hash.description: Reserved for a possible future dispatch-time read of roster/runner-capabilities.json (idea #8). Not populated by this schema version: the manifest is build/generator-time only today and is already transitively covered by catalog_content_hash, so populating this without an actual causal read path would misrepresent what produced the plan.

agentic_sdlc_contract_version.description: The lifecycle-gates contract's own version integer, recorded only when lifecycle_tracking.status is "integrated". Records which already-consumed, already-version-checked external contract shape Cadre's own code used -- not an assertion about the agentic-sdlc kernel's own repository/commit identity, gate-approval state, or run-record validity (see the two-repo boundary in AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md).
